newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton buyers need cover ahead of new crops.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton buyers need cover ahead of new crops.

text.p: German cotton consumers are looking for varied raw material cover ahead of new 1997/98, but supply is not always sufficient, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said on Monday.
Some of the nearby high grades required by the industry were not available and West African shipments were late.
Old crop supply was restricted to northern hemisphere material.
The Exchange reported upland turnover for 1997 dates in Central Asian standards 1 and 2, West African, Argentine, Pakistani and Australian cotton.
Syrian high grades traded for the second and third quarter of 1997 while Israel-Acala and El Paso/Mexico-Juarez Acala deals were completed through first quarter 1998.
Cotton stocks as of April 18 totalled 45,980 bales, down from 131,628 a year earlier and compared with 44,876 bales on April 4.
